newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Troops guard Durres port, test roads in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Troops guard Durres port, test roads in Albania.

text.p: French and Spanish troops from a multinational security force guarded this Albanian port and inspected roads on Wednesday on the first day of their mission to guarantee aid convoys.

French armoured personnel carriers (APCs) sped from this dismal city on the Adriatic to the capital Tirana, past armed police checkpoints, testing the road and bridges before convoys of humanitarian aid fan out across Albania on Friday.

"We're examining the bridges to make sure there's no chance they'll collapse when heavy aid convoys cross over," French army captain P. Noel told Reuters at the port where small groups of heavily armed infantrymen patrolled.
Captain Campello, who didn't give his first name, said: "We've been busy today protecting a U.N. food delivery."
Port workers unloaded from a Greek-owned ship some 400 tonnes of wheat flour and beans, sent by the U.N.'s World Food Programme (WFP), to a warehouse guarded by French soldiers.
The arrival of the humanitarian aid coincided with the landing on Tuesday of some 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish marines, who mostly came ashore at Durres.
The Italian-led eight-nation mission, which will eventually number 6,000 soldiers, will protect aid deliveries.
Nearly 300 people have been killed since the failure earlier this year of fraudulent investment plans in which many Albanians had invested life savings.
French and Spanish soldiers jointly control Durres port and set up camp beside a beach near the city, where they were busy checking their APCs before lining up for lunch.
One French officer at Durres port said he worried about banditry. Other troops had seen several suspicious transactions in the area involving the exchange of large sums of cash.
French infantrymen bivouacked overnight on Tuesday and many sat hunched in sleeping bags against the walls of shabby port buildings near the WFP vessel on Wednesday morning.
While French soldiers checked the road between Durres and Tirana, Albanian police wearing black masks and armed with Kalashnikov rifles conducted spot checks on passing cars.
Albanian APCs were stationed at some police checkpoints.

Captain Noel said the French soldiers would remain in Durres for the time being and were not expecting any push to the rebel-held south of the country, where many residents blame President Sali Berisha for the collapse of the savings plans.
"So far things are going smoothly. We are securing the port and this morning did reconnaissance on the Tirana road. No one has acted aggressively against us," he said.
French army captain Frank Parrera, whose unit was inspecting the bridges and roads between Tirana and Durres, said: "Everyone seems to be quite happy to see us here."
The first Greek troops in the multinational force landed at Tirana airport on Wednesday and headed for the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, officials said.

"One hundred and twenty soldiers, mainly infantry, are coming today. Two military aircraft have landed so far. Another four planes are expected later," Dimitris Moustaklis, a spokesman at the Greek embassy in Tirana, told Reuters.
In Athens, defence ministry sources said the soldiers were flown in C-130 planes from the northern city of Salonika to Tirana and the navy ship Samos sailed with another 130 troops.
The Samos, which is also carrying tanks, is expected to reach Vlore on Friday.
Forces from Turkey, Romania, Austria and Denmark are due to arrive over the next three weeks.
